editorial_thesis: Fresh platform changes favor a disciplined operating loop: route work by economics, keep delegated delivery reviewable, turn visual feedback into staged code change, and pin the build assumptions underneath it.

topic_groups.title: Agent Routing Economics
topic_groups.selection_rationale: A same-day OpenAI price and latency update materially changes the economics of high-volume agent work; this is a concrete update to the model-choice lane covered July 29, not a repeat of its earlier policy framing.

sources.title: Advancing the price-performance frontier with GPT-5.6
sources.why_selected: OpenAI cut Luna API pricing by 80% and Terra by 20%, while introducing Sol Fast mode at a stated 2× price for up to 2.5× speed.
sources.usefulness: Makes a measured task-tier routing pilot cheaper to run and easier to justify.

sources.title: GPT-5.6: Frontier intelligence that scales with your ambition
sources.why_selected: The product page defines the family roles and the Responses API tool-calling context for the pricing change.
sources.usefulness: Supplies a practical division of labor for planning, execution, testing, and evaluation.

topic_groups.title: Reviewable Delegated Delivery
topic_groups.selection_rationale: GitHub stacks and Linear’s new review/coding-session surfaces are fresh, complementary delivery controls. The lane deliberately shifts from last week’s agent governance toward the human review bottleneck created by parallel implementation.

sources.title: Stacked pull requests are now in public preview
sources.why_selected: GitHub now supports dependency-ordered PR layers that retain existing checks and branch protections.
sources.usefulness: Lets an agent or developer land a large feature as small independently reviewable units.

sources.title: Coding sessions on mobile
sources.why_selected: Linear adds mobile session steering, GA Guided Reviews, GitHub-team review assignment, and signed commits for coding sessions.
sources.usefulness: Makes delegated implementation visible and steerable without turning mobile access into blind approval.

topic_groups.title: Visual Design-to-Code Feedback
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Figma Make’s July 30 properties panel and canvas annotations are a material delivery update after the July 27 design-production coverage: edits can now be staged visually and applied to underlying code with targeted context.

sources.title: A Properties Panel and Annotations, Now in Figma Make
sources.why_selected: Figma Make adds direct visual property editing and marked-canvas instructions that apply to underlying code.
sources.usefulness: Offers a lower-ambiguity way to turn client feedback into staged, inspectable implementation changes.

topic_groups.title: Reproducible Build Boundaries
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Two July 30 platform changes expose build assumptions that are usually implicit: Cloudflare changed its default Node runtime, while GitHub added a same-commit reference for internal Actions. This is a practical infrastructure lane absent from recent coverage.

sources.title: Node.js 24 is now the default for Workers Builds
sources.why_selected: Workers Builds now defaults to Node.js 24.18.0, with 22.23.2 and 24.18.0 preinstalled.
sources.usefulness: Prompts an immediate audit of projects that rely on an unpinned Cloudflare build runtime.

sources.title: Reference same-repository actions with self-repository syntax
sources.why_selected: The new $/ syntax resolves an internal action or reusable workflow at the executing commit, without checkout.
sources.usefulness: Keeps internal CI composition aligned with full-SHA-pinning policy and avoids path/check-out coupling.

sources.title: Using pre-written building blocks in your workflow
sources.why_selected: Official documentation specifies $/ as the recommended same-repository syntax and records GHES limits.
sources.usefulness: Provides the migration reference and the important portability caveat.
